outputs.name: image
outputs.basis: the float image (before write_graphics truncates it) within 1 grey level of the frozen B200 output (tol 1 - d0, d0 = max |B200 - verify.py's CPU reference|). |a - g| <= 1 implies |trunc a - trunc g| <= 1 at every pixel, so the rule is stricter than verify.py's own check (max <= 3, <= 0.1 % of the pixels off by more than 1; verify.py:78-81), which make still requires of the CPU validation. Measured 2026-10-28: legitimate variants within 0.11 (9x below the limit), the closest wrong candidate (an fp16 image) 1.51, a stale q0sqr 7.3. The performance inputs' share clause (pixels off by >= 1) is not used here -- legitimate float32 summation orders of the statistic move up to 0.14 % of this image's pixels across an integer (Rodinia 3.1 OpenMP) while staying within 0.11 grey levels (README "Correctness probe")
